The Blackstone makes weekend breakfast easy and fun. I can cook the sausage, vegetables, and eggs at the same time so everything is hot and ready together. With 8 kids, that makes busy Saturday mornings much easier, and a toppings bar lets everyone build their tacos exactly how they like them.

Why You’ll Love This Recipe!

  • Budget Friendly Breakfast — $7.85 total for 12 street tacos
  • Everything cooks on one griddle at the same time
  • Set up a toppings bar with salsa avocado jalapeños and hot sauce
  • Ready in 20 minutes
  • Perfect for weekend breakfasts

If you love easy Blackstone breakfast recipes like this one you will also love our Blackstone Breakfast Burritos, Blackstone Scrambled Eggs, and Blackstone Hashbrowns Recipe.They are all budget-friendly, made with simple ingredients, and the kind of impressive griddle breakfasts your family will request every single weekend.

Why the Blackstone Makes Better Breakfast Tacos

The Blackstone flat top griddle is perfect for breakfast tacos because you can cook everything at the same time using different heat zones.

Cook the sausage and vegetables over medium high heat, scramble the eggs over lower heat, and warm the tortillas on the hottest section. Everything is ready at once, and the griddle gives the tortillas lightly charred spots that add great flavor.

Ingredients

  • Large eggs — whisked with milk salt and pepper until frothy before cooking. The milk adds richness and helps create softer fluffier scrambled eggs on the griddle
  • Milk — whisked into the eggs for a softer creamier scramble. Whole milk gives the richest result
  • Coarse sea salt and black pepper — essential seasoning whisked directly into the eggs before cooking
  • Oil — for the egg cooking zone on the griddle. A neutral high smoke point oil prevents sticking without burning at medium-low heat
  • Breakfast sausage — browned and crumbled alongside the vegetables. Spicy sausage gives extra heat — mild works for a family-friendly version. Crumbled bacon or chorizo work as great substitutes
  • Bell pepper, diced — adds sweetness color and texture to the sausage mixture. Any color works — red gives the sweetest flavor
  • Small onion, diced — cooked with the sausage and bell pepper for a savory aromatic depth throughout the filling
  • Salsa — spoon over the top of each taco right before serving for a fresh bright finish. Use your favorite store-bought brand
  • Colby Jack cheese, shredded — melts beautifully over the warm egg and sausage mixture. Freshly shredded melts more smoothly than pre-shredded. Pepper Jack adds heat for spice lovers
  • Avocado, diced — adds creamy richness that balances the bold sausage and egg flavors. Dice right before serving so it does not brown
  • Fresh cilantro — chopped and sprinkled over the top for a bright herby finish. Skip if your family is not a cilantro fan
  • Street taco tortillas — small flour tortillas that are the perfect size for handheld breakfast tacos. Warm and lightly char on the griddle before filling

Optional Add-Ins

  • Diced jalapeños — for heat lovers who want a kick in every bite
  • Sliced green onions — a mild fresh onion flavor that adds color and crunch
  • Crumbled cooked bacon — add alongside the sausage for an extra smoky protein punch
  • Diced tomatoes — a fresh juicy topping that brightens every bite
  • Hot sauce — set out on the side and let everyone add their own preferred amount
  • Pepper Jack cheese — swap for Colby Jack for extra heat throughout

How to Make Blackstone Breakfast Tacos

Step 1 – In a medium bowl, whisk together 6 large eggs, ¼ cup milk, ¼ teaspoon coarse sea salt, and ⅛ teaspoon ground black pepper until well combined and slightly frothy.

Step 2 – Preheat a Blackstone griddle to medium-high heat. Add ½ pound breakfast sausage, 1 diced bell pepper, and 1 diced small onion to one side of the griddle. Cook for 5 to 7 minutes, breaking up the sausage as it cooks, until the sausage is browned and the vegetables are tender.

Step 3 – Drizzle 1 tablespoon oil onto the other side of the griddle and reduce that section to medium-low heat.

Step 4 – Pour the egg mixture onto the oiled side of the griddle. As the eggs begin to set, use a spatula to gently pull the cooked eggs from the edges toward the center. Continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until the eggs are set but still soft.

Step 5 – Stir the cooked sausage, bell pepper, and onion mixture into the eggs and reduce the heat to low.

Step 6 – Place 12 street taco tortillas on the hotter side of the griddle and warm for about 30 seconds per side, or until soft and pliable.

Step 7 – Divide the sausage and egg mixture evenly among the 12 warmed tortillas.

Step 8 – Top the tacos with ½ cup shredded Colby Jack cheese, ⅓ cup salsa, 1 diced avocado, and 2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro.

Add any desired optional toppings, including diced jalapeños, sliced green onions, crumbled cooked bacon, diced tomatoes, hot sauce, or Pepper Jack cheese. Serve immediately.

Tips for Success

  • Cook eggs on medium-low heat. Low and slow scrambled eggs on the Blackstone give you a soft creamy result — high heat creates dry rubbery eggs that do not belong in a breakfast taco
  • Use the multi-zone method. Sausage on medium-high, eggs on medium-low, and tortillas on the hottest section — everything finishes at the same time without any juggling
  • Lightly char the tortillas. Those golden char marks add a smoky flavor that makes these taste authentic — 30 seconds per side on the hot zone is all it takes
  • Dice the avocado last. Avocado browns quickly once cut — always dice right before assembling the tacos for the freshest most vibrant result
  • Rotate tortillas for even browning. Every Blackstone has slight hot spots — rotate the tortillas halfway through warming for even color on all sides
  • Serve immediately. Breakfast tacos are best eaten straight from the griddle while the eggs are soft the cheese is melted and the tortillas are still warm and pliable

Variations and Substitutions

  • Swap breakfast sausage for chorizo for a spicier more flavorful filling with an authentic Mexican-inspired twist
  • Use corn tortillas instead of flour street taco tortillas for a gluten free option
  • Add diced breakfast potatoes to the sausage zone for a heartier more filling taco
  • Swap Colby Jack for pepper jack for extra heat or queso fresco for a more traditional flavor
  • Make it vegetarian by skipping the sausage and doubling the bell peppers and onions
  • Add a smear of refried beans inside each tortilla before the egg mixture for extra heartiness

Storage and Freezer Instructions

Refrigerator

  • Store the sausage and egg mixture separately from the tortillas and toppings in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Assemble fresh tacos when ready to serve for the best texture

Freezer

  • Not recommended for assembled tacos — the eggs and avocado do not freeze well. Make fresh batches as needed

Reheating

  • Reheat the sausage and egg mixture in a skillet over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes or microwave in 30-second intervals until just warmed through — always warm fresh tortillas on the Blackstone or in a dry skillet before assembling

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I make these without a Blackstone griddle?

Yes — use a large skillet or cast iron pan over medium heat. Cook the sausage and vegetables in one pan and the eggs in another for the same result without the griddle.

How do I keep the scrambled eggs from getting rubbery?

Cook on medium-low heat and remove from the griddle when they are just barely set — the residual heat finishes cooking them perfectly and keeps them soft and creamy.

Can I use flour tortillas instead of street taco tortillas?

Yes — standard flour tortillas work well but street taco tortillas are smaller and the perfect handheld size for breakfast tacos. Warm thoroughly before filling so they do not crack.

What is the best cheese for breakfast tacos?

Colby Jack melts beautifully and gives a mild crowd-pleasing flavor — pepper jack adds heat and queso fresco gives a more authentic Mexican-inspired result.

Can I make the filling ahead of time?

Yes — cook the sausage and egg mixture up to 3 days ahead and refrigerate. Reheat gently before assembling fresh tacos with warm tortillas and cold toppings.

How do I prevent the tortillas from cracking?

Always warm them thoroughly on the griddle for 30 seconds per side — cold tortillas crack immediately when folded around the filling. Lightly charring also adds flexibility.

Ingredients

  • 6 large eggs
  • ¼ cup milk
  • ¼ teaspoon coarse sea salt
  • ⅛ teaspoon ground black pepper
  • 1 tablespoon oil
  • ½ pound breakfast sausage
  • 1 bell pepper diced
  • 1 small onion diced
  • ⅓ cup salsa
  • ½ cup shredded Colby Jack Sheese
  • 1 avocado diced
  • 2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro
  • 12 street taco tortillas
  • Optional Add-Ins
  • Diced jalapeños
  • Sliced green onions
  • Crumbled cooked bacon
  • Diced tomatoes
  • Hot sauce
  • Pepper Jack cheese for extra heat

Instructions

  • In a medium bowl, whisk together large eggs, milk, coarse sea salt, and ground black pepper until well combined and slightly frothy.
  • Preheat a Blackstone griddle to medium-high heat.
  • Add breakfast sausage, diced bell pepper, and diced small onion to one side of the griddle. Cook for 5 to 7 minutes, breaking up the sausage as it cooks, until the sausage is browned and the vegetables are tender.
  • Drizzle 1 tablespoon oil onto the other side of the griddle and reduce that section to medium-low heat.
  • Pour the egg mixture onto the oiled side of the griddle. As the eggs begin to set, use a spatula to gently pull the cooked eggs from the edges toward the center. Continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until the eggs are set but still soft.
  • Stir the cooked sausage, bell pepper, and onion mixture into the eggs and reduce the heat to low.
  • Place 12 street taco tortillas on the hotter side of the griddle and warm for about 30 seconds per side, or until soft and pliable.
  • Divide the sausage and egg mixture evenly among the 12 warmed tortillas.
  • Top the tacos with shredded Colby Jack cheese, salsa, diced avocado, and chopped fresh cilantro.
  • Add any desired optional toppings, including diced jalapeños, sliced green onions, crumbled cooked bacon, diced tomatoes, hot sauce, or Pepper Jack cheese.
  • Serve immediately.

Recipe Notes

Warm tortillas are less likely to crack and hold the fillings better. For extra flavor, lightly char the tortillas on the griddle before assembling the tacos.
Freshly shredded mozzarella melts more smoothly than pre-shredded cheese.
If your griddle has hot spots, rotate the tortillas as they warm to prevent over-browning.
Leftover sausage and egg mixture can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 3 days.
